player.speaker: Front Commissar
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.reaction-briliant.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.reaction-briliant.text: The Tisza crossing succeeded. I will not pretend the staff expected it - the Romanian command certainly did not.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.reaction-tactical.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.reaction-tactical.text: The offensive has stopped on the far bank. I need fresh orders for the formations there before the Romanian counterattack reaches them.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.reaction-victory.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.reaction-victory.text: We hold a bridgehead. Whether it can be supplied across a river under observed artillery is the only question that now matters.
line.extra-alternate-history.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.extra-alternate-history.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.extra-alternate-history.text: The army survived the evacuation from Slovakia and has crossed the Tisza. That gives us a chance Paris and Bucharest didn't expect. It doesn't give us much time to repair this position.
line.callback-advance-deep.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.callback-advance-deep.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-advance-deep.text: The advance went beyond Szolnok, farther than we planned. Check those leading formations first. I need to know which roads they can use coming back.
line.callback-bridgehead-only.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.callback-bridgehead-only.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-bridgehead-only.text: We hold a bridgehead and no more. The crossing succeeded; the exploitation did not.
line.callback-committed-deep.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.callback-committed-deep.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-committed-deep.text: We committed the reserve deep, as you ordered. There is nothing left behind the line to commit again.
line.callback-held-central.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.callback-held-central.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-held-central.text: The central reserve is still available. Landler wanted it across sooner; now he's asking where we'll commit it. I need that decision before the next crossing report arrives.
line.telephone-lines-fail.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.telephone-lines-fail.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.telephone-lines-fail.text: Try the east-bank headquarters again. Some telephone lines have been shelled; others reach offices the staff has already left. I can't place the divisions from these reports. Send runners along the roads we still hold.
line.julier-opening.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.julier-opening.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.julier-opening.text: The divisions east of Szolnok are exhausted. Ammunition isn't crossing fast enough, and Romanian formations are gathering for a counterattack. We have to shorten the position or begin moving units back.
line.landler-question.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-question.text: Some reports say the Romanians knew our advance routes. We can investigate how later. For now: send the last reserve into the eastern bridgehead, or start withdrawing before they reach the crossings?
line.landler-question.choice.hold-east-b: Hold the eastern bridgehead with every available reserve and deny the enemy the initiative.
Gain a larger prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo the withdrawal's full resupply.
line.landler-question.choice.phased-with: Withdraw the most exhausted units first and build a final defence around the crossings on the west bank.
Fully resupply every core formation and gain a smaller prestige award, but forgo the final stand's core-wide experience.
line.julier-hold.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.julier-hold.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.julier-hold.text: Then shorten the perimeter and mass the guns. Do not defend empty ground. The bridgehead survives only if its flanks and the bridge itself remain under one command.
line.landler-hold-warning.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-hold-warning.text: I'll pass the order. Tell me how the shortened bridgehead will be supplied. The reserve cannot hold it for long if we can't get ammunition across.
line.landler-withdraw.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-withdraw.text: A withdrawal may save the army, but it must begin before the enemy reaches the bridges. Mark the order of movement now and leave disciplined rear guards, not abandoned battalions.
line.julier-withdraw-warning.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.julier-withdraw-warning.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.julier-withdraw-warning.text: After Slovakia, some regiments will hear this as another abandonment. Their officers must receive the movement order before the rumours do. I'll speak to them, but I need the crossing times from you.
line.kun-crisis.speaker: Béla Kun
line.kun-crisis.text: Budapest is hearing that whole headquarters have disappeared. Foreign missions are waiting for the government to fall. Keep enough of the army together to protect our people if the enemy reaches the capital.
line.landler-final.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-final.text: Hold those three points while the fresh Romanian formations come up. The bridges and guns need one command. No counterattack unless it helps us keep the line connected.
epilogue.east-bank-victory.speaker: Ferenc Julier
epilogue.east-bank-victory.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
epilogue.east-bank-victory.text: The bridgehead held. For several days I could still issue orders and know where the formations were. It wasn't enough to save the Republic. Landler is speaking to the survivors about their stand. I have to tell them which reserves and guns will not be coming back.
epilogue.east-bank-defeat.speaker: Jenő Landler
epilogue.east-bank-defeat.text: The last reserve was lost with the eastern bridgehead. We had no formed troops here to cover the fugitives. The White Terror is beginning, and men keep asking why we committed their comrades after the position could no longer be held. We owe them an answer.
epilogue.west-bank-victory.speaker: Béla Kun
epilogue.west-bank-victory.text: The army crossed back in order. It couldn't keep the Governing Council in power; after 1 August it had no state to defend. Some battalions could still escort threatened comrades and conceal weapons. Find the officers who stayed with them. Those connections may keep people alive.
epilogue.west-bank-defeat.speaker: Ferenc Julier
epilogue.west-bank-defeat.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
epilogue.west-bank-defeat.text: We started too late. Battalions reached the west bank separately, and I couldn't assemble them. With the White Terror beginning, some of those men may still escort or hide comrades. I can no longer promise them organised protection.
